items.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: Tony was best remembered, or he is probably best remembered in history for having done some of the English Peter Sellers movies with Hank mancini.

ctx.x: Or you say I don’t want to play that one. That’s interesting.

Now in 1980 I did an album which is also in the can with a wonderful English saxophonist and clarinetist, Tony Coe. Tony was best remembered, or he is probably best remembered in history for having done some of the English Peter Sellers movies with Hank Mancini. But I heard him play a couple of love ballads for me and then I went to an avante garde concert where he played with Derek Bailey, who is the English equivalent of Anton Webern and plays jazz. It was unbelievable. And I said that’s my guy. So I took Tony…
Wow. And it must have given the blues a certain amount of — I’m not sure what — finality or when you finally got there.
